statement: Which ordered pair $(x, y)$ is a solution to the system of inequalities below? $$\begin{aligned} y &> 2x - 3 \\ x + y &\le 6 \end{aligned}$$

choices.misconception: I treated $y > 2x - 3$ as if it allowed equality; for $(3, 3)$ the two sides are both 3, so the strict inequality is false.
I only checked the first inequality, which $(4, 6)$ satisfies, but $4 + 6 = 10$ is more than 6.
I only checked the second inequality, which $(5, 1)$ satisfies because $5 + 1 = 6$, but $1$ is not greater than $2(5) - 3 = 7$.

hints: A solution must make both inequalities true.
Substitute each ordered pair into both inequalities and watch for the strict $>$ sign.

solutions.reliable: Test each pair in both inequalities. $(3, 3)$: $3 > 3$ is false. $(4, 6)$: $6 > 5$ is true but $10 \le 6$ is false. $(5, 1)$: $1 > 7$ is false. $(1, 4)$: $4 > -1$ is true and $5 \le 6$ is true. Only $(1, 4)$ satisfies both.
